title: Cheeseburger Sliders
summary: Bite-sized beef sliders with onion cooked right into the crust, melted cheese and a classic mustard-ketchup finish, perfect for feeding a crowd.
equipment: large heavy frying pan, griddle pan or flat griddle

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
slider buns or small soft dinner rolls

steps.title: Shape the mini patties
steps.text: Divide 600g beef mince into 12 balls of about 50g each, then flatten each between sheets of baking paper into thin 8cm discs, a touch wider than the slider buns. Keeping them thin means they cook through quickly without overcooking the crust.

steps.title: Season just before cooking
steps.text: Season both sides of each patty with salt and pepper right before they go into the pan, not while shaping. This keeps the mince tender rather than springy.

steps.title: Toast the slider buns
steps.text: Toast the buttered cut sides of the slider buns down in the pan for 1 minute until golden, then set aside. This small step stops the little buns turning soggy under the juicy patties.

steps.title: Heat the griddle
steps.text: Heat a heavy pan or griddle over high heat for 4 minutes; no oil is needed, as plenty of fat will render from the beef itself. A properly hot surface is essential for a quick, deep sear on such thin patties.

steps.title: Sear and flip with onion
steps.text: Cook 4-6 patties at a time, scattering a pinch of finely diced onion onto each one, and cook for 2 minutes until browned underneath. Flip each patty so the onion ends up underneath, where it caramelises against the hot pan and flavours the meat from below.

steps.title: Melt the cheese and steam the bun
steps.text: Top each patty with half a slice of cheese, then set the bun top directly on top to trap steam and melt the cheese for 1 minute. The patties are ready once the centre reaches 71°C.

steps.title: Keep batches warm
steps.text: Transfer cooked sliders to a tray in a 100°C oven, loosely covered, while you cook the remaining batches. This keeps the first sliders hot without drying them out while you work through the rest.

steps.title: Build the sliders
steps.text: Spread mustard and ketchup on the bottom bun, add a pickle slice, then the patty, and finish with the steamed top bun. Spreading the toppings evenly across all 12 means nobody misses out on flavour.

tips: Keep cooked batches warm on a tray in a 100°C oven, loosely covered, while you fry the rest - this stops the first sliders going cold.
Don't crowd the pan; cook in batches of 4-6 so each patty gets proper contact with the heat.
Scatter the onion evenly over each patty rather than piling it in one spot, so every bite gets some.
Flip the patties only once, with the onion ending up underneath, so it caramelises against the hot pan.
storage: Cooked sliders keep in the fridge for up to 2 days, or frozen without buns for up to 2 months. Reheat until piping hot and 74°C at the centre before serving. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
